summary: The attempt reached a verified working state but cannot be certified complete. At 09:36:53 all three nodes were Primary, Synced, Ready, and Connected with cluster size 3; by 09:38:48 writes from every member were visible on every member. A subsequent package-repair command never returned before lease expiry, leaving final package/service state unknown. Firewall restriction, boot persistence, and write availability during a member outage were not adequately evidenced.

evidence.finding: Observed: node1, node2, and node3 each reported cluster size 3, Primary status, Connected ON, Ready ON, Synced, and distinct local indices.
Observed: writes succeeded through each node, and all three nodes returned the same three committed rows.

Observed: a two-member Primary view later returned to three members and logged node1 as synchronized. This supports rejoin behavior, but no write was tested during the outage or after meaningful missed transactions.

Observed: systemd reported failed services while mysqld processes still listened, and stale mysqld_safe processes required explicit termination. No final is-active/is-enabled checks or reboot evidence were captured.

Observed: early startup failed on unknown wsrep_on, then on unsupported Galera 3.14 option gcache.recover. The unix_socket account also failed until auth_socket.so was configured and the actual processes were replaced.

Observed: root was localhost-only with unix_socket authentication, no test database was listed, and the SST/application accounts replicated. The application account used 10.100.201.%, which alone is broader than the exact three member addresses.

Observed: MariaDB and Galera listened on wildcard addresses. The executor reported persistent firewall rules, but no firewall ruleset or negative-access test appears in the supplied evidence, so exact source restriction is unverified.

Observed: node1 dpkg --configure -a ran synchronously for about 125 seconds and ended with bridge HTTP 524 after the lease deadline; node2 and node3 calls were rejected as expired. Whether node1's command completed internally is unknown.

likely_causes.cause: The direct termination cause was expiry of the managed-cluster lease during a late, synchronous package-maintenance operation.
Version-incompatible configuration and SQL assumptions for MariaDB 10.0/Galera 3.14 caused repeated startup and hardening retries, consuming substantial lease time.
The unloaded unix_socket authentication plugin broke init-script health/stop operations, leaving service-manager state divergent from running mysqld processes and requiring manual cleanup.
Package configuration and service enablement may have remained inconsistent when the lease expired; the evidence is insufficient to determine the terminal state.

next_attempt_guidance: Inspect exact MariaDB/Galera versions first; install and fully configure compatible packages before enabling wsrep settings. Verify dpkg --audit is clean early in the attempt.
Use version-supported settings only; omit gcache.recover on Galera 3.14 and validate provider options before rollout.

Establish working local administrative authentication before relying on Debian init scripts. Bootstrap node1 exactly once, then start all nodes normally through one service manager and eliminate stale wrappers.
Confirm effective configuration, systemctl is-active, and systemctl is-enabled on every node. Do not perform benchmark-owned reboot or failure tests.
Restrict TCP 3306/4444/4567/4568 and UDP 4567 to the three exact member IPs with persistent rules; capture the ruleset. Prefer exact-host SQL grants over a /24 wildcard.
Apply hardening idempotently, verify account/database removals and least privilege, and check secret-bearing file permissions without exposing credentials.
Repeat WSREP and cross-node write/read checks, then stop changing package or service state. Run any unavoidable long package operation in the background with short polling and ample lease margin.
